hint.text: An allusion is used when an author wants to indirectly reference something. Allusions are often used in one story to reference another well-known literary, mythical or Biblical tale.

atoms.sound: Omari is as strong as Hercules
He is so romantic, like a true Romeo

atoms.a: Camilla volunteers weekly at the homeless shelter;
atoms.sound: Camilla volunteers weekly at the homeless shelter; she’s a Good Samaritan.

hint.text:
• In the Bible’s Story of Job, Job is described as a very patient man.

• In Greek mythology, King Midas could turn anything he touched into gold.

• Siri is a virtual assistant that can answer almost any question.
hint.sound:
• In the Bible’s Story of Jobe, Jobe is described as a very patient man.

• In Greek mythology, King Midas could turn anything he touched into gold.

• Siri is a virtual assistant that can answer almost any question.

atoms.a: Ask Donovan anything and he’ll know the answer.
atoms.sound: Ask Donovan anything, and he’ll know the answer. He’s the real-life Siri!

atoms.b: I may as well call you Job.
atoms.sound: You are incredibly patient; I may as well call you Jobe.

atoms.a: My aunt finds success wherever she goes.
atoms.sound: My aunt finds success wherever she goes. She’s got the Midas touch!

instruction.text: Read the allusion and then choose what it implies.

atoms.a: The new nature reserve is like a Garden of Eden for animals.
